A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Octopus research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching reordered case studies.

before.justification: V1 reports original model-training experiments, benchmark evaluations, component ablations, training diagnostics and self-correction case studies.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds text-only benchmark results and comparative inference-cost measurements.

M1.justification: Rollout recombination and selection, mixed-sampling cold-start training, two-stage response masking, objectives and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. The corrected delimiter spelling in Appendix A.1 does not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Section 5.4 and new Figure 8 extend evaluation from multimodal inputs to text-only mathematical reasoning on AIME2024 and language understanding on MMLU-Pro. This substantially broadens the tested input domain; existing training datasets and seven multimodal benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged. The added evaluations reuse existing comparators, including the Qwen base model, GRPO, GSPO and SRPO; no new comparison method is introduced.

E3.justification: Appendix B.2 introduces an evaluation reporting average inference time and output-token count on MathVista. Existing splits, sampling parameters, training budgets and token limits remain unchanged. Specific splits and sample counts for the new text-only evaluations are not documented.

E4.justification: Figure 8 adds a transfer analysis comparing performance before and after self-correction on text-only inputs, while Appendix B.2 examines the inference overhead of producing two responses. Existing component ablations, training-collapse diagnostics and all four case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added results continue point-estimate reporting; average inference measurements do not introduce run-to-run uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V2 adds supplementary results: Figure 8 reports Octopus o1/o2 accuracies of 81.4/85.7 on MMLU-Pro and 40.0/46.7 on AIME2024. Table 6 adds inference measurements, including 166 seconds and 1063 tokens for Octopus. Its MathVista accuracy of 82.1 repeats the existing result; original benchmark and ablation values are unchanged.

T1.justification: The self-correction definition, reward formulations and optimization equations are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about rollout augmentation, response masking, seven-benchmark performance and 0.72× training time. The added evaluations do not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.4 newly interprets text-only transfer as evidence of modality-agnostic self-correction. Appendix B.2 attributes comparable inference latency to similar output lengths. However, the statement that baselines fail to improve text-only performance overgeneralizes Figure 8: MMLU-Pro baseline scores improve from 71.6 to 80.0–81.4.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 restores the missing closing angle bracket in the written self-correction opening tag, making the delimiter consistent with the existing prompts. Training hyperparameters, frameworks, hardware disclosure and project access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for AIME2024 and MMLU-Pro. Related-work positioning remains unchanged; the Sherlock reference receives publication metadata updates rather than being replaced by a different work.

P1.justification: V2 adds short transfer and inference-efficiency passages, subdivides Appendix B, adds acknowledgements and a generic impact statement, and updates the publication footer. Most prose and the main section sequence are preserved.

P2.justification: V2 adds the text-only comparison plot as Figure 8 and inference-efficiency Table 6. The existing failure plot moves and becomes Figure 9; the first two case studies exchange order, and appendix displays are redistributed across pages. Existing scientific displays otherwise remain intact.

improvement.justification: The added inference-cost comparison addresses a gap in v1's efficiency evidence, while text-only evaluations provide useful evidence about transfer beyond visual inputs. These are limited gains: the new evaluations lack detailed protocol documentation, and the blanket statement about baseline degradation conflicts with MMLU-Pro results. Overall, the additions modestly strengthen the paper without changing its central method or established results.
